```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load necessary libraries
library(stm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(SnowballC)
library(tm)
library(textmineR)
library(wordcloud)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


# Structural Topic Modeling (STM) Using `stm` Package

```{r, include=TRUE}
# Load the dataset
# https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/therohk/million-headlines/data
# This contains data of news headlines published over a period of nineteen years.
# Sourced from the reputable Australian news source ABC (Australian Broadcasting Corporation)
# Agency Site: (http://www.abc.net.au)

news_data <- read.csv("data/abcnews-date-text.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dim(news_data)
str(news_data)

# Extract year and month and then convert to decimal year
news_data$publish_date = as.Date(as.character(news_data$publish_date), format = "%Y%m%d")
news_data$year <- as.numeric(format(news_data$publish_date, "%Y"))
news_data$month <- as.numeric(format(news_data$publish_date, "%m"))
news_data$date <- news_data$year + (news_data$month - 1) / 12
head(news_data)
```


```{r, include=TRUE}
# Can take a small sub-sample. Comment this line out if want to use all observations:
set.seed(1258)
news_data <- sample_frac(news_data, 0.05)

# Extract documents and metadata
documents <- news_data$headline_text
meta <- data.frame(date = news_data$date)
```

```{r, include=TRUE}
# Preprocess text data
processed <- textProcessor(documents = documents, metadata = meta, lowercase = TRUE)
out <- prepDocuments(processed$documents, processed$vocab, processed$meta)
# saveRDS(processed, "processed.rds")
# saveRDS(out, "out.rds")
# processed <- readRDS("processed.rds")
# out <- readRDS("out.rds")

# Assign preprocessed data to variables
docs <- out$documents
vocab <- out$vocab
meta <- out$meta
```

```{r}
# Fit the STM model, including date as a covariate. Assume 5 topics.
stm_model <- stm(documents = docs, vocab = vocab, K = 5, 
                 prevalence = ~ date,
                 data = meta, 
                 max.em.its = 75, 
                 init.type = "Spectral")
```

```{r, fig.width=10}
# Summarize the STM model
summary(stm_model)
```


```{r, fig.width=10}
# Visualize the prevalence of topics, highlighting the five most representative words for each topic
plot(stm_model, type = "summary", n = 5)
```

```{r, fig.width=10}
# Plot word clouds for each topic
par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(.1, .1, .1, .1))
for (topic in 1:5) {
  cloud(stm_model, topic = topic, scale = c(2, 0.5), max.words = 50, colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))
}
```

```{r}
# Estimate effects of date on topic prevalence
effects <- estimateEffect(1:5 ~ date, stmobj = stm_model, metadata = meta, uncertainty = "Global")
```

```{r}
# Plot the effects with confidence intervals
plot(effects, covariate = "date", topics = 1:5, model = stm_model,
     method = "continuous", xlab = "Date", main = "Effect of Publication Date on Topics")
```



# What if We Did Not Know the Number of Topics?

```{r}
# Finding optimal number of topics
K_result <- searchK(out$documents, out$vocab, K = seq(2, 10), prevalence = ~ date, data = out$meta)
plot(K_result)
```

```{r}
# Plotting Coherence vs. Exclusivity
coherence <- sapply(K_result$results$semcoh, function(x) x[1])
exclusivity <- sapply(K_result$results$exclus, function(x) x[1])
K_values <- seq(2, 10)
plot_data <- data.frame(Topics = K_values, Coherence = coherence, Exclusivity = exclusivity)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Exclusivity, y = Coherence, label = Topics)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.5) +
  labs(title = "Exclusivity vs. Coherence", x = "Exclusivity", y = "Semantic Coherence") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# How to Select the Best Run for a Given Number of Topics? 

```{r}
# Use selectModel to find the best run with a specific K
best_model <- selectModel(out$documents, out$vocab, K = 5, 
                          prevalence = ~ date, data = out$meta, 
                          runs = 20, seed = 12345)

# Plot model diagnostics using plotModels to visualize coherence and exclusivity; customize point symbols and place legend
plotModels(best_model, pch=c(1,2,3,4), legend.position="bottomright")

# Choose the best initialization
selected_model <- best_model$runout[[2]]

# Summarize the selected model
summary(selected_model)
```
